newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK ECON MIN REACHES FOR COMPROMISE WITH PROPOSALS.
newsitem.headline: GREEK ECON MIN REACHES FOR COMPROMISE WITH PROPOSALS.

text.p: Greek National Economy Minister Yannos Papandoniou announced late on Tuesday a series of measures aimed at a compromise with the brokers association, which has refused to trade, accusing the government of a cover-up.
His ministry said in a statement that the bourse's clearing house would cover Delta Securities' 2.6 billion drachma default and would submit immediate payment to the state National Bank.
He also said the clearing house would be in turn entitled to claim the funds it will pay from member Delta Securities and the bourse's guarantee fund.

Consistent with an earlier announcement by the capital markets commission, all trades will have to be fully settled by the morning of Thursday November 14. All members who fail to settle with the clearing house will not be allowed to trade.
Their failure to settle will be a violation of stock exchange regulations, the statement said.
Furthermore, any other defaults that may arise after total settlement will be covered by the exchange's guarantee fund which will submit the funds to the clearing house.
The guarantee fund will be entitled to claim the funds it is called to pay from all relevant parties as the law foresees.
The capital markets commission may call for an extra assessment by brokers to enable it the guarantee fund to cover any defaults that may arise from trades up to November 7.

It seemed that the crisis was heading towards a solution as sources at the brokers association told Reuters that its members had agreed with the proposals in principle and that trade at the Athens bourse could start late on Wednesday and resume normally on Thursday.
"It's not entirely what we were asking for but we consider it a realistic solution to try and find a way out to the deadlock," said Alexander Moraitakis managing director of Nuntius Securities.

He added that the fact that henceforth brokerages would not receive payment on executed sell orders before delivering shares would render all members more careful and was encouraging. --George Georgiopoulos, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
